arxiv-2206-09187.title: Why most molecular clouds are gravitationally dominated 2015 Why most molecular clouds are gravitationally dominated – References
arxiv-2206-09187.creator: Laura Ramírez-Galeano, Javier Ballesteros-Paredes, Rowan J. Smith, Vianey Camacho & Manuel Zamora-Avilés
arxiv-2206-09187.description: Abstract Observational and theoretical evidence suggests that a substantial population of molecular clouds (MCs) appear to be unbound, dominated by turbulent motions. However, these estimations are made typically via the so-called viral parameter α vir class \alpha_{\rm vir}^{\rm class} , which is an observational proxy to the virial ratio between the kinetic and the gravitational energy.

arxiv-2411-10330.title: CNN-Based Classification of Persian Miniature Paintings from Five Renowned Schools
arxiv-2411-10330.creator: Mojtaba Shahi, Roozbeh Rajabi, Farnaz Masoumzadeh
arxiv-2411-10330.description: Abstract This article addresses the gap in computational painting analysis focused on Persian miniature painting, a rich cultural and artistic heritage. It introduces a novel approach using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to classify Persian miniatures from five schools: Herat, Tabriz-e Avval, Shiraz-e Avval, Tabriz-e Dovvom, and Qajar. The method achieves an average accuracy of over 91%.

pmc-12459562.description: This study aimed to provide evidence for the development of targeted interventions by investigating the current status of osteoporosis prevention health behaviors and their impact factors in older patients with hip fragility fractures. pmc-12473908.title: A Comparative Study of the Effect of Commonly Used Pesticides on Cervical Contractions in Pregnant Cows, In Vitro
pmc-12473908.creator: Michal Hubert Wrobel, Zhenghong Zuo, Minjian Chen
pmc-12473908.description: Organochlorine insecticides (DDTs), organophosphate insecticides (malathion), carbamate insecticides (carbaryl and thiram), pyrethroid (cypermethrin and fenvalarate) insecticides, and herbicides (glyphosate and atrazine) were selected for this study because they disrupt cervical and myometrial function in the bovine oestrous cycle. However, their potential to affect reproductive success in cattle during pregnancy has not been directly confirmed.

pmc-12617247.title: Classifying Internet Addiction Using Machine Learning Approach: A Study Among Adolescents in Bangladesh
pmc-12617247.creator: Akher Ali, Md Sahadat Hosain, Md Abu Bakkar Siddik, Mahedi Hasan, Md Ahashan Habib, Mohammad Alamgir Kabir, Mohammad Mizanur Rahman, Peal Ahamed Shanto, Nafiul Hasan, Al Mahmud
pmc-12617247.description: BackgroundInternet addiction (IA) among adolescents is growing worldwide. Online temptation is particularly strong for adolescents due to rapid physical and cognitive development. IA may impair their mental, emotional, social, and physical health. Few traditional studies were conducted in Bangladesh. Thus, this study aimed to identify adolescents’ IA risk factors using advanced machine learning (ML).

pmc-12846669.title: Porcine Cytomegalovirus/Porcine Roseolovirus, Previously Transmitted During Xenotransplantation, Does Not Infect Human 293T and Mouse Cells with Impaired Antiviral Defense
pmc-12846669.creator: Hina Jhelum, Reinhold Schäfer, Benedikt B. Kaufer, Joachim Denner
pmc-12846669.description: Porcine cytomegalovirus, more accurately classified as porcine roseolovirus (PCMV/PRV), was shown to be pathogenic in the context of xenotransplantation. Transmission of PCMV/PRV to non-human primates receiving hearts or kidneys from virus-positive pigs significantly reduced the survival time of the recipients. PCMV/PRV was also transmitted to the first human recipient of a pig heart transplant and contributed to the patient’s death.

pmc-13245609.title: Proximity‐Induced Transfer of a Mass Tag Enables Direct Profiling of Active Matrix Metalloproteases
pmc-13245609.creator: Lomane Berthy, Ugo Pasco, Mylene Sejalon‐Cipolla, Pierrick Bruyat, Monika Kaminska, Carole Malgorn, Fabrice Beau, Manca Osolin, Metka Novak, Barbara Breznik, Dimitris Georgiadis, Isabelle Correia, Emeline Groult, Olivier Lequin, Sarah Bregant, Yves‐Marie Pers, Daniele Noel, Robert Thai, Gilles Subra
pmc-13245609.description: Conventional activity‐based probes in activity‐based protein profiling (ABPP) require enrichment or reporter tags for detection, which limits sensitivity and multiplexing. Here, we present an enrichment‐free chemoproteomic approach that enables direct mass spectrometric detection by Matrix‐Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization (MALDI) of active proteases.

pmc-13279260.title: Data-driven prioritization of high-risk individuals for weight loss interventions
pmc-13279260.creator: Kamil Demircan, Julia Carrasco-Zanini, Alice Williamson, Carl Beuchel, Linsey Jackson, Werner Römisch-Margl, Aleksander L Hansen, Sarah Finer, David A van Heel, Genes & Health Research Team, Gabi Kastenmüller, Matthew Coghlan, Ida Moeller, Nicholas J Wareham, Maik Pietzner, Claudia Langenberg
pmc-13279260.description: New obesity medications have demonstrated efficacy in trials, but their real-world deployment is partly limited by the absence of approaches that identify individuals for treatment based on risks for obesity-related complications. Here we present a risk prediction model to guide prioritization of high-risk individuals.

pmc-13474526.title: Targeted delivery of mRNA to immune cells for in vivo cell therapy
pmc-13474526.creator: Danyang Wang, Yumin Li, Jinfeng Deng, Mengxin Li, Lin-Ping Wu
pmc-13474526.description: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have revolutionized biomedicine by enabling direct in vivo programming of immune cells. This strategy bypasses the complex manufacturing and high costs associated with ex vivo cell therapies. However, efficient and specific systemic delivery of mRNA to target immune cell subsets remains a major translational hurdle. This review systematically examines engineering strategies that address this challenge.
